2026-08-28T05:49:37.5180688Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5181193Z 
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5181562Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5182631Z 
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5183610Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5184272Z 
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5187039Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5192434Z >
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5195422Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5201054Z >
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5202046Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5203048Z 
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5203236Z ### How to Use
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5203521Z 
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5204507Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5205586Z 
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5205781Z ```bash
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5206540Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5207630Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5208371Z ```
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5208611Z 
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5208903Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5209541Z ```bash
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5210167Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5211106Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5212110Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5213016Z ```
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5213258Z 
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5213996Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5215089Z ```bash
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5215730Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5216554Z ```
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5216781Z 
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5217549Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5218292Z ```bash
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5218899Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5219962Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5220819Z ```
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5221053Z 
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5221350Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5221873Z 
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5223681Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5225828Z 
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5226014Z ```bash
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5226525Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5227722Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5228764Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5229141Z 
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5229685Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5230918Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5231932Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5232471Z ```
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5232700Z 
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5233612Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5234818Z 
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5234997Z ```bash
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5235772Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5236866Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5237896Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5238445Z 
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5238917Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5239888Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5240533Z ```
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5240769Z 
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5241018Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5241982Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5243183Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5244371Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5246101Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5250797Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5253157Z 
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5253379Z ### Notes
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5255113Z 
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5257543Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5262380Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5271452Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5273148Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5274686Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5277131Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5278904Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5279772Z </mcp-clis>
2026-08-28T05:49:37.5280213Z <github-context>
